prerequisite.development: Authorized to continue while acceptance is pending

P11.1: Six separate named public schemas from API design section 4.7, with exact attribute sets, explicit indexes, a coarse ocean-basin allowlist and bounded readonly publication options.
Independent read-only Rabdi adapter using pinned @arkiv-network/sdk 1.0.1, expected creator and current owner, creation flags and expiration.
Bounded task-index lookup filtered by schema, task and wallet. Reports query block, observed head, lag and truncation.
P11.2: Operator adapter publishes task and claim intents with exact public attributes and independently pinned requester and claimant wallets. Claims require a current matching task record.

Each wallet serializes its writes in a durable operator-owned directory. A reservation binds the task or claim intent to a predicted entity key before broadcast. Replays read the reserved key and compare attributes. An ambiguous send or inconsistent key keeps the writer fenced for operator review.
The existing ORCA assignment service was exercised with two separately keyed A2A providers. Each had a distinct claim on the same task, and concurrent assignment attempts produced one winner.

Authenticated task creation supports an explicitly approved Arkiv v1 companion. The provider discovery command can publish a matching claim companion from its wallet. Import validates the signed claim and the v1 record against the same pinned provider.
The worker publishes an Arkiv v1 assignment companion with the selected claim key and signed assignment digest before A2A dispatch. Existing signed records preserve the established execution checks.
P11.3: An authenticated project operator can approve and export a minimal publication intent derived from a completed, signed artifact. A review requires an independently owned signer and wallet, a public source result, and the same accepted result digest.

The producer or reviewer publishes from its own wallet through the existing durable writer. A separate read API queries by expected digest and owner, matches the exact public attributes, excludes expired rows, and exposes a bounded key cursor and index lag.
The Provenance tab displays saved signed task history and paginated current Arkiv result or review observations. It exposes explicit consent before exporting the operator intent.
P11.4: The independent verifier runs without the ORCA API. It checks expected public attributes and wallet ownership, and can compare RFC 8785 artifact bytes with the approved digest.

Reconciliation checks a known transaction against its current canonical block and the pinned engine's creation event. Missing or changed receipts cannot promote a held intent, and current absence is reported separately from recorded expiry.
The Rabdi reader bounds rate-limit backoff and the legacy recovery tool refuses to requeue Arkiv v1 operations.

local_checks: Five focused P11.2 Node tests passed for separate writers, duplicate claims, uncertain sends, read-only recovery, and a mismatched returned key.
Two PostgreSQL integration cases passed using loopback PostGIS and local provider processes, covering competing claims and the existing worker hold after an ambiguous chain submission.
A later 13-test Node run covered the public schema and outbox, including rejection of an assignment targeting a different claim binding and read-only replay of an accepted assignment reference.

The authenticated HTTP-to-worker integration passed against loopback PostGIS with simulated Arkiv transport. It verified consent gating, exact selected provider attributes, persistence of the task receipt, and assignment companion creation before the intercepted A2A dispatch.

27 focused Node tests passed across the public schema, outbox and dashboard. Two PostgreSQL integration tests passed with separately keyed local A2A processes and simulated Arkiv indexing, including rejection of a private source result, a shared reviewer wallet, substituted attributes, and expired records.

All 54 Arkiv and ENS Node tests passed. Four Python unit tests and two PostgreSQL worker regressions passed. The worker regressions verify that both the legacy writer and Arkiv v1 remain held after an uncertain write.

wallet_balance_status.evidence: Public RPC confirmed nonzero balances for the previously published H04 requester and provider addresses.

result_query.note: A successful read-only query for a historical H04 digest and wallet established current RPC support for the result query. There was no new P11 result entity to verify.

live_read_only.note: The query checks a historical H04 task ID against the new P11 schema. The result establishes RPC compatibility with the query. Public balances do not establish signer control or institutional eligibility. No P11 transaction was sent and no P11 record was read back.

remaining.P11.1: Verify live P11 schema writes and current readback with authorized, separately controlled test wallets.
remaining.P11.2: Verify the authenticated opt-in path with separately controlled Rabdi wallets and live task, claim and assignment receipts. Institutional eligibility still requires reviewed G10 trust policy. Operator review and read-only CLI reconciliation cover uncertain writes; authenticated recovery of held operations remains open.
remaining.P11.3: Run the signed-in dashboard against separately owned live P11 result and review receipts. Operator-side publication uses the exported intent and existing standalone writer.
remaining.P11.4: Verify an active P11 entity independently while the ORCA API is offline. Capture authorized live multi-wallet lifecycle and recovery evidence. Add authenticated requeue of held operations only after positive readback of all required publications.
